spans.s:
Jyeṣṭha, ordinarily meaning ‘greatest,’ has further the specific sense of ‘eldest’ brother in the Rigveda. It also means the eldest among sons, which is another side of the same sense.
Foot notes With changed accent, jyeṣṭhá. Cf. Macdonell, Vedic Grammar, p. 83, 14.
iv. 33, 5; x. 11, 2.
Av. xii. 2, 35; aitareya brāhmaṇa, vii. 17; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xi. 5, 3, 8, and cf. Jyaiṣthineya.

Jyeṣṭha-ghnī, ‘slaying the eldest,’ is the name of a nakṣatra, or lunar mansion, usually called jyeṣṭhā, in the Atharvaveda and the taittirīya brāhmaṇa. It is Antares or Cor Scipionis.
Foot notes vi. 110, 2. Cf. vi. 112, 1.
i. 5, 2, 8. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 361.
